_readme: Curated 'seen in fiction' overlay for real exoplanet systems. This file is NOT generated by the pipeline and is intentionally kept OUT of planets.json. Merge later by joining `systems[].planets[].archive_name` to the `name` field in data/planets.json. Every system in `systems` has at least one CONFIRMED planet in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (verified 2026-07-24 against the pscomppars TAP table), so it appears — or will appear on a larger `pipeline build --bulk N` pull — in the ~6k known-exoplanet catalog and can carry a physics-derived colour. The `star_only_cameos` block at the bottom is separate: those famous fictional worlds map to real STARS that have NO confirmed planet, so they are absent from the archive and cannot get an albedo/colour swatch. Do not merge cameos into planet records.
_join: systems[].planets[].archive_name == planets.json .name. `in_current_planets_json` marks whether it is already in the committed 953-planet subset (true) or only appears after a larger archive pull (false).
_honesty: Fiction fame only — science-news fame (glass-rain planet, diamond planet, NASA travel posters) is deliberately excluded per the project's dual-audience / honest-wording principle. Confidence flags note weak/name-drop or unverified references.
source: NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars TAP) for confirmation; fiction references hand-curated and sourced.

star_only_cameos._note: These famous fictional worlds map to real STARS with NO confirmed planet in the NASA Exoplanet Archive. They will NOT appear in the ~6k catalog at any bulk size and cannot get a physics-derived colour (no planet = no albedo). Keep them separate: if ever shown, they must be a flagged 'fictional cameo — star only, no measured planet' card, never a real swatch.
